### Offset-notification configuration inventory

Bearer-authenticated `POST /v2/notifications/offset/list` inventories user-created offset-notification configurations and returns at most 400 records per request. Optional body `cursor` paginates, while `archive_filter` accepts archived, non-archived, or all configurations and defaults to non-archived; HTTP `200` requires `data` and may expose nullable sibling `cursor`. Each item requires configuration identity, name, type, environment, creator, creation time, nullable archive time, and a policy whose required lifecycle-event type and ISO-8601 offset distinguish before-event from after-event schedules. The endpoint defines no event-type catalog, ordering, total count, cursor completion or lifetime, stable snapshot, freshness, calculated fire time, generation state, delivery state, or history completeness. It lists configurations only and does not establish creation, edit, archival transition, event enablement, generation, webhook delivery, or reconciliation behavior. [[source-metronome-api-reference-notifications-list-offset-lifecycle-event-notification-configurations]]
warnings: Keep configuration inventory distinct from scheduling execution and webhook delivery authority.
Do not infer a complete event-type catalog or stable inventory from cursor exhaustion.
Preserve body cursor placement and the default NOT_ARCHIVED filter.

concepts.proposed_markdown: For offset-notification configuration audits, bearer-authenticated `POST /v2/notifications/offset/list` returns user-created lifecycle-relative configurations with a maximum of 400 results per request. Body `cursor` and optional nullable response `cursor` are endpoint-specific pagination surfaces; the archive filter defaults to non-archived. Returned records expose identity, environment, creation and archive metadata, plus lifecycle-event type and signed ISO-8601 offset, but not calculated fire time, generation outcome, delivery state, webhook destination, or event history. The endpoint defines no ordering, total count, cursor completion or lifetime, stable snapshot, duplicate-or-skip behavior during changes, as-of marker, freshness, or read-after-mutation visibility. Complete traversal therefore cannot by itself prove a point-in-time configuration inventory, schedule execution, delivery completeness, or cross-system reconciliation. [[source-metronome-api-reference-notifications-list-offset-lifecycle-event-notification-configurations]]
warnings: Treat the endpoint as configuration-audit inventory, not notification-delivery or reconciliation reporting.
Do not substitute the generic query next_page traversal contract for this endpoint's body and response cursor.

concepts.proposed_markdown: - [[source-metronome-api-reference-notifications-list-offset-lifecycle-event-notification-configurations]] - offset-notification configuration audit, archive-state filtering, endpoint-specific pagination, and ordering, snapshot, freshness, delivery, and reconciliation boundaries

`POST /v2/notifications/offset/list` is a paginated configuration read under the separate API-wide `Idempotency-Key` authority. A provided-key result is persisted only after execution admission; identical same-key parameters then replay that original result rather than prove a fresh offset-configuration inventory or stable pagination snapshot. Changing body `limit`, `cursor`, or `archive_filter` changes parameters, so reuse of the same key returns HTTP `409` under the API-wide contract. The endpoint does not require the header, prescribe a key policy across pages, or add local error, cursor-lifetime, cache-freshness, concurrency, read-after-mutation, propagation, another-key, expired-key, or recovery behavior. [[source-metronome-api-reference-notifications-list-offset-lifecycle-event-notification-configurations]] [[source-metronome-api-reference-idempotency]]
warnings: Keep execution admission and changed-parameter behavior sourced to the separate API-wide idempotency authority.
Do not treat same-key replay as a fresh configuration audit or infer a preferred key-per-page policy.
